title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
layout_note: A small square, column-width diagram: one input circle at the bottom centre forks up-left and up-right into two view circles; above each a vertical stack (network, then head boxes) rises to an output circle at the top. The loss is a centred text line between the two outputs, with no box.
grouping: No containers or background panels. The two columns are mirror images: left = student, right = teacher, each a stack of rectangles. The teacher column holds one extra box (centering) between its network and its softmax. A thin horizontal arrow labelled 'ema' runs between the two network boxes from student to teacher.
shapes_depth: Flat, monochrome. The two networks are sharp-cornered rectangles filled light grey; the head operations (softmax, centering) are white rectangles with thin black outlines; inputs, views and outputs are outlined circles with a serif symbol (x, x1, x2, p1, p2). All text is set in one serif face. Thin black arrows; the teacher's arrow into its output circle is crossed by a double slash labelled 'sg'.
proposed_highlight: The method is shown, not highlighted: student and teacher get identical grey boxes distinguished only by their names and subscripts, and the training-specific parts are small marks on the teacher side (the extra centering box, the sg double slash, the ema arrow coming in from the student).
lesson: Draw the two networks as identical grey boxes and mark everything that makes them differ as small inline glyphs on the teacher column (an extra head box, an sg double slash on its output edge, an 'ema' arrow from the student), so the asymmetry is readable without colour.
notes: venue and year as recorded by Semantic Scholar.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: Two mirrored vertical branches, student on the left and teacher on the right, rising from a single input x at the bottom centre that splits into two views x1 and x2.
insights.data: Variables (x, x1, x2, p1, p2) are circles, networks are grey-filled boxes (student g_theta_s, teacher g_theta_t), and post-processing steps are white boxes (softmax; centering + softmax on the teacher).
insights.emphasis: Asymmetry between the branches is the point: only the teacher has an extra 'centering' box and a double-slash 'sg' stop-gradient mark, and a horizontal 'ema' arrow runs from student to teacher.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: x splits by two diagonal arrows into the views, each passes up its branch to p1 / p2, and the cross-entropy 'loss: - p2 log p1' is written as text between the two outputs at the top.
insights.avoid: The loss is only floating text with no lines joining p1 and p2, so the comparison point is implied rather than drawn.

arrangement.units: Two unframed vertical branches (student, teacher) of stacked boxes, side by side.
arrangement.inputs_as: a single circled x splitting into two circled views x1, x2
arrangement.losses_at: top centre, as a text formula between p1 and p2
arrangement.shared: teacher is an EMA of the student, shown by a horizontal 'ema' arrow between the network boxes
